videos.title: Mr Eazi on Comfort, Molly, TikTok & Business vs Music | Cool Nigerian Vibes with DJ Rabbit
videos.headline: Mr Eazi on Comfort, Molly, TikTok & Business vs Music | Cool Nigerian Vibes with DJ Rabbit
videos.description:
Mr Eazi sits down with DJ Rabbit on Cool Nigerian Vibes for a candid conversation about his hit single “Comfort” featuring Moliy, the viral teaser that used a Splice sample, his playful TikTok rebrand, and why music remains his foundation even as he builds businesses.
In this exclusive interview, Mr Eazi opens up about:
•  How he created “Comfort” and why he flew Moliy to London after the teaser
•  His sudden lively, dancing personality on TikTok and the “50 shades of Mr. Eazi” across platforms
•  Choosing between a global hit and building companies that impact millions of Africans
•  Why his biggest legacy will always be the music (comparing it to Jay-Z)
•  Openness to collaborations with young artists and a new song dropping in four weeks
Stream “Comfort” by Mr Eazi ft. Moliy now.
Follow Mr Eazi on TikTok: @mistereazi
This is Cool Nigerian Vibes with DJ Rabbit. Stay tuned for more Afrobeats, interviews, and exclusive music talk.

videos.title: “Men must also be careful with how affectionate and intimate they are with their daughters.”— Vector
videos.headline: “Men must also be careful with how affectionate and intimate they are with their daughters.”— Vector
videos.description:
Vector returns with a deeply introspective track dedicated to fathers and daughters. In this exclusive Cool FM interview and live unplugged performance, the legendary Nigerian rapper, songwriter, and lyricist (known for his deep, reflective style) breaks down the inspiration behind “Dad & Dot,” released in support of the International Day of the Girl Child.
“Dot” represents the daughter. The song addresses father presence (and absence), emotional connection, boundaries, love, and the realities of raising daughters in today’s Nigeria — moving beyond pure “vibes” to music that reflects society.
Highlights from the conversation:
•  Vector on the role of the artist to observe and report
•  Why the song felt timely and how Cynthia (his daughter’s aunt) came on the hook
•  Emotional moments while recording
•  Thoughts on affection, protection, and bonding between Nigerian fathers and daughters
•  Why hip-hop should balance entertainment with meaningful messages
Live Performance:
Vector and Cynthia deliver a powerful, emotional unplugged rendition of “Dad & Dot” — a rare live radio moment.
Key Themes: Fatherhood • Daughters • Introspective Nigerian Rap • International Day of the Girl Child • Deep Lyrics • Cool FM
Lyrics excerpt:
“I pray that you only see love at the end anyway / Know in your life I’ll be there to defend anyway… Baby, I may be mean anytime, anywhere, any day / Just know that I love you a lot in a damn heavy way.”

videos.title: Tunde Onakoya: From Ikorodu Slums to Lagos International Chess Festival 2026–2027
videos.headline: Tunde Onakoya: From Ikorodu Slums to Lagos International Chess Festival 2026–2027
videos.description:
Tunde Onakoya opens up on Cool FM about how chess saved his life in the Ikorodu ghetto and why he’s bringing the world to Lagos with the Lagos International Chess Festival (October 2026 – October 2027).
In this powerful interview, the Chess in Slums founder shares his journey from dropping out of school to winning scholarships, breaking the world record in Times Square, and now launching an ambitious year-long festival that makes chess cool, social, and accessible to everyone.
What’s coming in the Lagos International Chess Festival:

•  Chess on boats & yachts
•  Chess + art exhibitions
•  Massive children’s tournaments (targeting 2,000 kids)
•  Beginners’ tournaments & Good Move Chess Club (every Tuesday)
•  Celebrity chess challenges (Burna Boy, Tems and others already play)
•  Chess & fashion events
•  Masters tournament with grandmasters
•  Afrobeat Chess Party (DJ + chessboards + live vibes)
Tunde talks about making chess a unifying social experience that connects people from the slums of Ikorodu to Lekki, Paris, and New York — while positioning Lagos as a global destination for the 500 million people who play chess worldwide.
Key moments:
•  How he discovered chess at a barbershop
•  Why service (not just the game) drives the Chess in Slums work
•  Full-circle moment returning to Cool FM after the Chess Is Lunch project
•  Why now is the perfect time for the festival
Follow Tunde Onakoya on all socials for festival dates, Good Move Chess Club details, and event updates.
If chess changed his life, imagine what it can do for a whole city.

videos.title: “She Said Yes! Diana Eneje Talks Proposal, Growing Up Online & Life at 24”
videos.headline: “She Said Yes! Diana Eneje Talks Proposal, Growing Up Online & Life at 24”
videos.description:
Diana Eneje (the original Dumebi) sits down with Mannie and Vanessa on Cool FM for a candid conversation about her journey — from posting church pictures on Instagram at 14 to becoming one of Nigeria’s most recognizable luxury lifestyle influencers, beauty entrepreneur, and content creator.
In this full interview, Diana opens up about being friends with Rema before he was signed, missing his first music video because of JAMB, being told her hips were “too wide” for signed modeling, growing up as the last born, the misconceptions people have about her “lucky” life, why she treats YouTube like a personal documentary, social media income, finding the right partner, and her recent surprise proposal.
In this video:
•  How she almost starred in Rema’s first video but had to prioritize JAMB
•  Becoming the face of Dumebi and the impact of the video
•  Starting Instagram at 14 and building an audience early
•  Growing up as the last of three and how her family shaped her boldness
•  The biggest misconceptions about her lifestyle
•  Why she sees YouTube as a long-form documentary of her life
•  Social media money, diversifying platforms, and the real work behind the glam
•  Advice on finding the right partner and working on yourself first
•  Her reaction to the proposal and rapid-fire questions

videos.title: Bluetopia Opens Up On Authenticity, Bloomy Ship with Temi, Family Drama & Life After BBNaija S11
videos.headline: Bluetopia Opens Up On Authenticity, Bloomy Ship with Temi, Family Drama & Life After BBNaija S11
videos.description:
Bluetopia (Banta Saku Karen / Usaku Keren Bantai) sits down for a candid post-show interview after finishing 4th place in BBNaija Season 11 “Show Ya Sef.” The face card of the season opens up about leaving Biggie’s house, watching herself through TikTok stickers and edits, staying 100% authentic, and the real friendships that carried her.
In this full interview, Bluetopia talks about:
•  How it felt stepping outside after weeks in the house and seeing fan reactions
•  Her crazy facial expressions that became viral stickers
•  Staying real with zero strategy (boarding school prepared her)
•  The Bloomy ship with Temi (pillow talks, shared interests, and becoming close late in the season)
•  The “Nuclear Family” with Sheba, Godessa, Abby, Temi and others — how it started and what viewers missed
•  Navigating alliances, week 5 anxiety, and the divide in the house
•  Post-show fallout with Sheba and why she hasn’t addressed the clip yet
•  The Oyin, Tram, and Kibo night
•  Her fans: Blue Rangers and Blueprints — and why their support shocked her
•  Future plans: runway modeling, London/Paris Fashion Week, launching her clothing brand, acting, and more
•  School, staying accessible to fans, and her message to the trolls
Bluetopia proved you can be fully yourself, wear your emotions on your sleeve, and still make top 5. This is the unfiltered conversation BBNaija fans have been waiting for.
